$about: The Protected List of `04-ux-flows.md` §7, made machine-readable.
§8: 'The Protected List is executable, or it is not protected.' Rule 1 there is
the one this file exists to enforce — NO MVP ITEM MAY BE MARKED DONE WHILE ITS
PROTECTED ASSERTION IS SKIPPED. Until this file existed there was nothing that
could tell 'covered by a test' apart from 'nobody has looked', which is exactly
the classic failure §8 describes: the feature ships, the test is disabled
'temporarily', and the detail is gone by the time anyone runs a demo.
So every item carries a STATUS and it is checked by scripts/protected-list.test.ts:
covered  — names a test id that must exist in the suite. A typo fails the build.
blocked  — names what blocks it. An empty blocker fails the build.
partial  — the feature exists in part; `missing` lists what does not, in words.
`partial` is deliberately NOT a passing state. It is here so a half-built item
reads as half-built instead of quietly counting as done, and so the gap is a
sentence somebody wrote rather than a silence somebody has to notice.

items.title: The kanban card as the whole status report — six facts without opening anything
missing: The card renders SIX of the seven facts in 04b 2.4: annualised premium, days untouched, the attempt count, the next activity, the health rail and the signal slot.

DONE: the fixed card height. Ruling N17's 120px desktop / 156px mobile is registered in ref.ci_ratchet with the pinned arm (migration 0024) and closed in two halves — card-height.test.ts ties the CSS token to the pinned number and proves AP004 refuses a different one, card-anatomy.spec.ts ties the token to what a browser renders and asserts a uniform column pitch. 04b carried three heights (108/92, 112, 120/156) before N17 struck two.
DONE: the attempt count, with zero rendering as `Not called yet` rather than `0 attempts`.

DONE: the health rail and the signal slot, both server-computed so the board, My Book and My Day cannot disagree. The rail is a GRADIENT, not a colour — it fills at days_since_touch divided by cold_threshold_days, which is the WCAG 1.4.1 second signal and the half a threshold-only design never shows. Exactly one signal per card, suppressed entirely on earning and lost stages (MVP item 32). The two precedence orders differ on purpose and a test asserts the difference: the rail is overdue-above-fresh (2.8), the slot is fresh-above-overdue (2.7). Two renderings per signal — `Going cold - 9d` on the face, the full sentence as the accessible name. 9 integration tests, 3 e2e, proved by mutation on both the precedence and the suppression.

DONE, and it was a live defect rather than a gap: app.tenant shipped rotting_threshold_days plus a CHECK ordering two decay thresholds — the pre-R6 two-tier design — with cold_threshold_days defaulting to 14 instead of the ruled 7. Migration 0025 drops it. Had the rail been built on it, going-cold would have fired a week late and red would have kept the second meaning R6 deletes it to prevent. CI check R2-6 now exists as a test.
Absent: lead source. lead_source_id is deliberately deferred to the intake module, so the chip has no column to read and 2.4 says it is not rendered rather than showing `Unknown`.

Absent: two of the six signal-slot entries. The recent-contact chip is priority 1 by design — ping-post sells the same consumer to two sellers inside an hour — and needs tenant-wide call history; `needs reply` needs inbound SMS. Both wait on Aloware. The `blocked` health state waits on the same gate.

Absent: the second half of the suppression rule — never on imported cards never worked. It needs `imported_at`, which arrives with intake. The day a CSV import lands, a thousand untouched cards go amber at once unless signalsSuppressed grows that clause.

Absent: the NEW clock TICKS, and this is now a MEASURED refusal rather than a deferral. 2.7 wants `NEW 04:12` counting client-side; the chip renders the shape correctly but does not advance. Built and reverted: on perf-500, where all 500 cards are fresh, ticking every chip cost a 116.7ms frame and an 84ms long task against budgets of 34 and 50. Scoping the tick to on-screen chips with a shared IntersectionObserver brought it to 50.0ms and 53.0ms — still over. P6 stays green only without it. The next attempt needs virtualization or a non-React DOM write, and starts from these numbers rather than from scratch.

items.title: Global owner-scoped search, Cmd/Ctrl+K, under 200ms perceived
missing: DONE: the server half. /api/search reads name, phone and email — the three fields search.idle names — owner-scoped for a seller and global with an owner chip on every row for a supervisor, with the role read from the seat rather than from anything the client sends.

DONE: E.164 normalisation. 937-555-0142, (937) 555-0142, 9375550142, +19375550142 and 1 937 555 0142 all find the record, and so do the last four digits. Normalisation is deliberately not validation: a typo returns nothing rather than being refused, and the empty state gets the number back.

DONE: the Ctrl/Cmd+K overlay, in the SHELL so it works from any surface — asserted on three. Focus lands in the input; arrows move the highlight while focus STAYS in the input; Enter opens the record; Escape closes and restores focus to whatever opened it, which is the rule everybody skips and the one a mouse never tests. Skeleton rows paint on the keystroke. All four states ship with their ratified strings: search.idle, search.empty, search.empty.supervisor and the error. axe clean on the open overlay with results showing.

DONE: the contact record the search opens, at /contacts/:id, with NO loader — ui.loader_whitelist is shrink_only and would refuse a fourth, so the engine forced the independent fetch §1.1 wanted anyway. A foreign id, a missing id and a malformed id are indistinguishable: all read `That contact isn't in your book`, never a 403. That is DEMO-04 on the screen a pasted URL actually lands on, asserted in the browser and in six integration tests.

🔬 RECORDED: opening the endpoint's own owner predicate to true left every test green, because contact's owner_scoped RLS policy had already scoped the rows. The silo is held by the database; the application predicate is the second layer. The tests prove the property, not which layer delivers it.

DONE: N13 — the server budget, MEASURED and enforced. 59.7ms p95 across 25,000 contacts in fifty books, registered at 120 in perf-budgets.json and in ref.ci_ratchet with the monotonic_down arm. The fixture asserts its own size before anything is timed (04b 3.6: an improvement caused by a smaller fixture fails), and the six queries are the ones §7 puts a seller in front of rather than synthetic ones. US-LCP-08's 500ms end-to-end is deliberately NOT ratcheted — P5.3 calls it a consequence, not a budget.

🔴 The first measurement was 1,053ms and nothing about the schema changed to fix it. Migration 0011 already had the right index — a composite GIN with the ownership predicate INSIDE it — and the query was written so it could not be used: scoping in a CTE and matching in a LATERAL forced a sequential scan of the tenant on every keystroke. 0011's comment names the deeper reason that index shape exists, and it is a silo property rather than a speed one.

DONE: `Quick-add this number` is a control now, and the loop §7 opens closes. The empty state's button opens a sheet with the number already normalised, prefilled and read-only — retyping it is the step that turns `add this lead` into `add it later`. Save lands on the contact record. Asserted end to end in the browser, from an empty search to a record with a name on it.

DONE: the duplicate is refused by a CONSTRAINT, never by a lookup. contact_phone_owner_uidx has been UNIQUE on (tenant_id, owner_user_id, phone_e164) since migration 0010, so a double-tapped Save or two open tabs lose the second write in the database rather than passing a check that raced. The endpoint's only job is turning that refusal into `You already have {name} with this number.` plus a way to open the record — the part a constraint cannot do. If the row is not readable it is somebody else's book, and it is reported WITHOUT a name: naming it would be a cross-silo disclosure wearing a helpful message.

🔴 Three defects the tests found, and each was invisible on the happy path. Drizzle rewraps the driver error, so the SQLSTATE sat one level down in `cause` and the constraint fired perfectly while the application could not tell — a designed refusal arriving as a 500. A violation ABORTS the transaction, so the recovery lookup that names the duplicate cannot run in the same one; catching a database refusal and then asking the database about it is always two units of work in Postgres. And `FormData.get` returns `string | File`, so `String(...)` would have written `[object File]` into a contact's name.

Partial: two of the four fields 4.11 ratifies are absent, and honestly. `lead_source_id` belongs to the intake module and the activity_type enum has no `note` member, so neither has a column to land in — a field that silently discards what a seller typed is worse than a field that is not there. `Save & call` is 4.11's primary and needs the Aloware gate, which does not exist; shipping a button that saves and does not call would be the one lie this sheet could tell.

Absent: the `under 200ms perceived` half of this item's own title. N13 measures the SERVER at 59.7ms p95 and the overlay paints skeletons on the keystroke, but nothing measures what a seller's eye actually waits for. That number is US-LCP-08's 500ms end-to-end, which P5.3 calls a consequence rather than a budget — so it is deliberately unratcheted, and this item stays partial because of it rather than in spite of it.

items.title: The honest go-live board: fifty names, fifty $0, the footnote, and the activity strip
missing: DONE: the board includes a seller with no ledger row at $0 (migration 0017 fixed the join that hid them); the permanent 'The board starts at go-live' footnote; the 'Earnings tracked since' label; and the 'Demo tenant — these numbers are seeded' note. All asserted by honest-board.spec.ts.

DONE: the four ratified per-period empty states (lb.empty.alltime/.today/.week/.month) plus lb.footnote.period_boundary. The four sentences are guarded mechanically by empty-copy.test.ts — a collapse back into one interpolated string fails the build — and board-periods.spec.ts asserts which tab shows the boundary footnote and that the period selector actually changes the board. The empty block hangs off the floor total, not off rows.length, because the roster join means rows is never empty once a tenant has sellers.

Absent: the today activity strip — dials, contacts, appointments set — which is the ONLY number that moves before the first sale. It counts from call.completed on any outcome, so it needs the Aloware module.

items.title: The first ten seconds: Demo chip, first-run checklist, My Day counts, rank and gap above the fold
missing: DONE: the rank-and-gap line above the fold on the seller home ('You're #2 · $9,029.88 · $2,550.12 to pass Priya N.'), asserted by rank-and-gap.spec.ts on BOTH profiles — the sentence's shape, its box inside the viewport, and its position ahead of the day's first section. The gap is subtracted on the server; tests/integration/leaderboard-standing.test.ts holds that half, including the tie and the $0 seller.

DONE: the persistent 'Demo' chip in the shell, which survives navigation across all three screens, and the seeded-numbers footnote on the board. Both asserted by honest-board.spec.ts, and the seed now sets tenant.is_demo.

DONE: the four-item first-run checklist, asserted by first-run-checklist.spec.ts — the ratified labels in order, the absence of any 'mark done' control, the auto-check reading real data, 44px rows, and the collapse at four of four. CAVEAT, stated rather than hidden: item 1 cannot complete because aloware_number_mapping does not exist, so the collapse is proven against a stubbed setup read, and item 4's granted path is proven against a stubbed Notification object because headless Chromium reports 'denied' whatever the test grants.
DONE earlier: My Day renders its four sections with counts in the header, and the seed is separately tenanted and refuses to run twice.

DONE, and neither was ever recorded as missing: the seed now SPANS ALL FOUR PERIODS and includes ONE REVERSAL, both named by §1529. Every seeded win used to land on now() because stage_move can only stamp now(), so day, week, month and all-time held one identical number and the period selector demonstrated nothing at minute 0:30. The first win of each seller still goes through the real gate; the rest are backdated through ledger_append, anchored to the CURRENT period boundaries in the tenant business timezone rather than to a fixed number of days.
Absent: the seed refuses to DUPLICATE but not to run in a live environment — that needs system_constant, which does not exist.
